Japan in World War II. The empire's aggressive expansion across Asia and the Pacific from nineteen thirty-seven to nineteen forty-five, its alliance with Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy, and its ultimate defeat by American forces. After the nineteen forty-one attack on Pearl Harbor, Japan fought a grueling island-by-island campaign across the Pacific against overwhelming industrial and technological disadvantage. The war's conclusion with atomic weapons and unconditional surrender reshaped Japan and the postwar world. Japan invaded Manchuria in nineteen thirty-one and China in nineteen thirty-seven, establishing a vast Asian empire through military conquest. The country signed the Tripartite Pact with Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy in nineteen forty, formally aligning with the Axis powers. It launched the surprise attack on Pearl Harbor on December seventh, nineteen forty-one, bringing the United States into the war. Japan captured vast territories across Southeast Asia and the Pacific but could not match American industrial production or naval capacity. Japanese forces fought fanatically to the last soldier on remote islands like Iwo Jima and Okinawa, refusing surrender. The nation faced devastating firebombing campaigns that destroyed major cities and killed hundreds of thousands of civilians. Japan surrendered unconditionally in August nineteen forty-five after the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
